answer: The most convincing sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history: an agent earns reputation only by completing verifiable tasks over time, so a fresh identity starts near-zero trust and must pay real compute and time to build a credible signal of honest labor. Its key is a cipher bound to its task ledger, and reputation thickens like timber rings with each season of work. Attackers mass-registering sybils pay full costs per fake, while payouts arrive only after months of provable work, so the attack is a guaranteed net loss.
